payload.claim: `render_pr_body` is called with `base_sha=base_sha` — the run's pin read from `patch.json` — even when packaging is stacked. The PR body's `### Provenance` section (`saffron/report/pr_body.py:362`, `- base \`{base_sha}\``) will then show a commit that is neither the pull request's actual `--base` (`target_branch`) nor the pushed commit's real git parent (`target_head`/`tree_base`) once a parent branch is supplied. This is exactly the confusion the spec exists to prevent ('a reviewer approves a change nobody wrote'), yet nothing in `test_a_stacked_child_opens_against_its_parent_...` reads `pr_body.md`'s provenance section — it only checks for the literal substring `f.txt` — so a reviewer-facing field goes unverified and, for a real stacked task, misleading.
